breakfast noun

also breakfast is ready

classical

Suet. Vit. 13 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 36, 38
Traupman 67
Traupman 70

1jentāculum: short e (Bennett’s hidden long ē, printed in an earlier version of this entry). From jentō; Lewis & Short leaves both unmarked (jentaculum, jento). The reading after Bennett was withdrawn on review. Ruling: jentāculum with a short e.

jentāculum1, jentāculī n.

noun, second declension

Examples

  • jentāculum parāre

    prepare breakfastcomposed

  • Jentāculum parō.

    I’m making breakfast.composed

  • Jentāculum est parātum.

    Breakfast is ready.Traupman 36

  • Vīsne sūmere jentāculum an prandium?

    Do you want to eat breakfast or lunch?Traupman 67

See also eat breakfast, lunch, cereal, porridge.

SourcesLewis & Short: jentaculum · Bennett: hidden quantities, with later corrections

The example sentences marked “composed” are ours.
